evals.prompt: Family Bridges of Chattanooga (family shelter, $2.1M budget) just got a new CoC RRH award of $640K plus some ESG RRH from the city. We need to serve about 45 families in year one. Median 2BR asking rent here is a bit above FMR. Can you help me write the RRH program design — who gets what, staffing, budget, and outcome targets?
evals.expected_output: An RRH program design document covering population/eligibility with coordinated entry and PSH screening, the three core components with a dedicated landlord liaison and caseloads, progressive engagement, a budget sized from medians, a privately funded risk-mitigation fund, outcome targets, and a written-standards crosswalk distinguishing CoC vs ESG rules.
assertions: Builds the design around the three RRH core components: housing identification, rental and move-in assistance, and voluntary case management

Distinguishes CoC and ESG RRH rules (e.g., ESG's 24-months-in-3-years limit and FMR/rent reasonableness; CoC deposit limits) and says local CoC written standards and ESG recipient caps override national defaults
Staffs a dedicated housing navigator/landlord liaison separate from case managers and states a case manager caseload range
Sizes the financial-assistance pool from expected medians rather than caps, and reports cost per household and cost per successful exit
Sets outcome targets including exits to permanent housing, days to move-in, returns to homelessness at 6/12/24 months, and unknown destinations under about 10%
Includes PSH screening at entry with coordinated entry as the referral path, and notes a knowledgeable staffer should check the design against current CoC written standards and HUD notices

evals.prompt: Our case managers in Boise are just cutting RRH rent help on a set schedule — 100% months 1-3, 50% months 4-6, then done. Families keep coming back to shelter. Need a progressive engagement assistance policy, short version.
evals.expected_output: A progressive-engagement financial assistance policy that starts with the least assistance, re-assesses at defined intervals, tapers only on documented income or rent-burden change, escalates in steps, tracks ESG cumulative months, and includes an exceptions process.
assertions: Replaces calendar-based step-downs with tapering only on documented income or rent-burden change
Starts with the least assistance that resolves the episode and escalates in steps (one-time help → partial subsidy → full time-limited subsidy) tied to documented need
Sets defined re-assessment intervals (e.g., 30/60/90 days then monthly), ideally generating tasks in HMIS
Includes tracking of cumulative months of ESG assistance against the 24-months-in-3-years limit with early flags
Includes documentation requirements per step plus taper/termination rules and an exceptions process, and notes monthly case manager contact is required but services are not a condition of assistance

evals.prompt: Our board in rural Garrett County, MD wants to convert our scattered-site RRH into an 18-month congregate transitional housing building for families, with mandatory sobriety and required life-skills classes, because 'RRH families aren't ready.' Several of our current families have a parent with serious mental illness who's been homeless for years. Write me the case for the board.
evals.expected_output: A TH-vs-RRH decision analysis for the named population using the matrix and Family Options evidence, noting legitimate TH signals (thin rural market) but warning that sobriety/required services produce poor exits, screening high-acuity long-homeless families for PSH first, and naming a metric that would prove the choice wrong.
assertions: Applies the TH-vs-RRH decision matrix dimensions (market depth, income, barrier type, safety, population evidence, cost per exit) to this specific population
Cites the HUD Family Options Study finding that RRH exited families from shelter faster and cheaper than project-based TH, with benchmark costs flagged as study-era dollars to inflate
Flags that families with a parent with serious mental illness and long homelessness should be screened for PSH first, which outranks the TH/RRH choice
Warns that making sobriety or services a condition of TH housing produces poor exits and that services should be voluntary
Acknowledges a thin rural rental market as a legitimate TH signal and names a monitoring metric (e.g., exits to permanent housing or length of stay) that would prove the choice wrong within a year

should_not_trigger.query: Plan our January Point-in-Time count: volunteers, canvass map, and survey instrument.
HUD is monitoring our CoC rapid rehousing grant next month — what files and APR documentation do they check?
